idiom_name: serde internally tagged command enum over a tokio mpsc channel or async broker client
implementation_notes: Rust's enum is the command type: variants carry their own fields and a match on the enum is checked exhaustively, while serde's internally tagged representation (#[serde(tag = "type")]) puts the discriminator into the wire payload in the shape Java-style APIs use - the variant set replaces the command class hierarchy and the compiler replaces the registry. In-process, commands travel on tokio::sync::mpsc (bounded, so back-pressure is real) to a single owner task; across processes the same enum is deserialized from a broker payload (rdkafka, async-nats). A trait-object hierarchy with dyn dispatch is worth it only when handlers must be registered dynamically at runtime, which is rare.
pitfalls: Serde's internally tagged representation rejects enums that contain tuple variants - a compile-time error - so command variants must be struct variants or use the adjacently tagged form (tag + content).
Internally tagged deserialization needs the alloc feature; in no_std without an allocator the command payload cannot be decoded.
A bounded channel pushes back on the sender while an unbounded one hides overload until memory grows; pick deliberately and propagate send errors instead of ignoring them.
